problem.heading: The problems facing agriculture
problem.subcopy: Gaps in information and technology between producers, distributors and consumers keep rural Latin America poor.

items.title: Technology
items.body: rural inhabitants in the region lack meaningful connectivity: with no signal or data, precision agriculture never reaches the farm.

items.title: Information
items.body: of farms in the region are family farms, and there is still no systematic data to measure their productivity.

items.title: Financing
items.body: of smallholder credit demand goes unmet: a US$170 billion gap.

gapItems.label: in crops and livestock are lost to disasters worldwide every year.

problem.exitKicker: The way out: digitize the producer
problem.exitBody: Their plot, with a track record for credit and insurance.
problem.sources: Sources: IICA, World Bank et al., Rural connectivity in LAC (2022) · FAO and UNDP, Family farming in LAC (2024) · ISF Advisors, Pathways to Prosperity (2019) · FAO, The Impact of Disasters on Agriculture and Food Security (2023), 1991–2021 average.

solutions.subcopy: We integrate the agri value chain's services so every player decides with the same data: complete, standardized, verified and processed.

items.name: Productive Score
items.body: An individual analytical system per plot and crop. It measures the productive strength of each active plot: climate, health and biological risks, historical productive strength and presence of deforestation.

items.name: Analytics licenses
items.body: A mobile app that digitizes the producer: standardized forms per crop, productive indicators and continuous alerts about their plot.

items.name: Regional Productive Analysis
items.body: Productive status by geographic zone, crop, segment (micro, SME, corporate) and cycle. For corporate, institutional and government clients.

items.name: Regional Climate Analysis
items.body: Satellite monitoring by agroclimatic zone (country, province, canton): rainfall and temperature anomalies, ENSO events, drought and flooding, crossed with portfolio exposure.

items.name: Ongoing training
items.body: Use of the digital tools and alert systems, crop control and development techniques, and best practices seen in other countries.

items.name: Automated dashboards
items.body: Dashboards that turn large volumes of data into visual, actionable stories, dynamically and on time. Powered by Power BI.

solutions.modelsHeading: Prediction and intelligence on climate and production data
solutions.modelsNote: We keep investing in domain-specific foundation models.

models.name: Crop detection
models.body: Crop area and estimated production by country, canton or plot.

models.name: Nitrogen uptake
models.body: Monitoring of the crop's nitrogen uptake.

models.name: Water stress

models.name: Disease
models.body: Early warnings of disease and pests.

models.name: Crop progress
models.body: Tracking of the crop's growth stage.

models.name: Yield forecast
models.body: Yield estimate up to maturity date.

ifis.heading: We are part of the whole credit analysis process
ifis.subcopy: From prospecting to collections, the same data supports every stage of the decision.

stages.name: Prospecting
stages.lead: Sector analysis by crop and producer prospecting.
stages.body: Where the universe is, what it grows and on how much land.

stages.name: Origination
stages.body: Amount, term and collateral set by the plot's risk band.

stages.name: Monitoring
stages.lead: Satellite monitoring and alerts on pledged plots.
stages.body: Stress, drought or waterlogging crossed with the repayment calendar.

stages.name: Collections
stages.body: Reschedule before the due date, not after default.

ifis.callout: We don't only come in at the end.
ifis.calloutBody: The same measurement that approves the loan monitors it during the cycle and anticipates collections: one productive source of repayment, auditable from start to finish.
ifis.scoreHeading: A rating of productive risk, not just financial risk
ifis.scoreSubcopy: Agri credit is repaid with the harvest: portfolio quality is the quality of the crops behind it.

scoreBlocks.name: What it measures
scoreBlocks.body: Eight productive blocks on the plot: soil and climate, crop and vigor, management, cycle history, territory and absorption capacity.

scoreBlocks.name: Analysis windows
scoreBlocks.body: History of previous cycles, the state of the current cycle and the projection up to the harvest that backs the installment.

scoreBlocks.name: How to read it
scoreBlocks.body: A 0–100 band: the higher the score, the lower the productive risk. Bands translate into decisions on amount, term and collateral.

scoreDecision.label: Delivered per producer and per plot
Re-read per cycle and per alert
Productive input for PD and LGD

ifis.scoreNote: The score doesn't replace the bank's model: it complements it with the productive source of repayment the financial model doesn't capture.
ifis.climateHeading: Climate risk is measured by agroclimatic zone, not by client
ifis.climateSubcopy: A portfolio diversified by client can still be concentrated in the same basin, crop and harvest calendar.

climateItems.name: Exposure map
points: Crosses the balance with the hazard by zone, crop and cycle
Exposed balance by basin and canton, not only by province

climateItems.name: Weekly zonal monitoring
points: Satellite reports on the zones where clients are
Alerts for extreme rainfall, drought and heat waves
A log of climate indicators for the institution

climateItems.name: ENSO stress test
points: Applies the 1997–98 El Niño scenario to today's portfolio
Incremental expected loss by zone and crop
Input for provisions and risk appetite

climateItems.name: Repayment calendar
points: Crosses each due date with the rainy-season window
Preventive collections triggered by crop condition

ifis.baselHeading: Basel already treats climate as a prudential risk on five fronts
ifis.baselSubcopy: The Basel Committee defines climate as a driver of the risks banks already manage: without climate variables, they can't measure or report them.

baselItems.name: Governance and appetite
baselItems.contribution: Exposure by agroclimatic zone, crop and cycle

baselItems.name: Credit risk
baselItems.requires: Climate in PD, LGD and collateral
baselItems.contribution: Plot georeference, hazard and crop condition

baselItems.name: Capital and liquidity
baselItems.contribution: Incremental expected loss per climate event

baselItems.name: Scenarios and stress
baselItems.contribution: 1997–98 ENSO scenario applied to today's portfolio

baselItems.name: Disclosure (Pillar 3)
baselItems.contribution: Exposed balance by province, canton and hazard

ifis.baselClosing: All five requirements start from the same data: the georeferenced portfolio crossed with each zone's climate hazard.
ifis.baselSources: BCBS, Principles for the effective management and supervision of climate-related financial risks (Jun 2022) · BCBS, A framework for the voluntary disclosure of climate-related financial risks (Jun 2025).
ifis.safeguard: Safeguard: the score complements the bank's model, it doesn't replace it. No adverse decision about a client rests on the climate signal alone; every decision keeps documented human review.

elNino.headingStart: El Niño 2026–27 is already in your portfolio.
elNino.body: We can start by measuring the real exposure of your agri portfolio: a concentration map by basin and canton, and the incremental expected loss on the current book.

actors.heading: The same data solves each player's pain point
actors.subcopy: Every digitized plot feeds the score, origination and territorial intelligence.

items.name: Producers and associations
items.pain: Produce without data and with little access to credit.
items.deliver: An app with pest, water-stress and weather alerts.

items.name: Banks and credit unions
items.pain: Agri delinquency of 9.88% at credit unions vs. 4.09% at banks (Jul 2026).
items.deliver: Productive score, yield forecast and traceability; real-time climate, productive, health and sustainability alerts.

items.name: Agribusiness and exporters
items.pain: Don't know what, where or how much will be harvested.

items.name: Government and multilaterals
items.pain: Design policies and insurance without territorial evidence.
items.deliver: Territorial intelligence by country, province and canton.

about.heading: A data-driven agri-fintech
about.body: InteliCrop is an agricultural analytics and technology company. We combine satellite imagery (200+ satellites, 3×3 m resolution and over 40 years of history), climate data and field data with AI models trained for more than 170 crops, 100% in the cloud.
about.body2: We put that intelligence to work for those who finance, buy, insure and regulate agriculture: financial institutions, agribusiness and exporters, governments, certifiers, associations and producers themselves.
about.cropin: Official CROPIN representative in Ecuador and LATAM

statements.name: Purpose
statements.body: Close the information gap between the field and capital so every producer is visible, measurable and financeable.

statements.name: Mission
statements.body: Drive farmers' development through a smart agricultural cloud that turns satellite, climate and field data into production, credit and sustainability decisions.

statements.name: Vision 2030
statements.body: Be Latin America's reference platform for measuring agricultural productive risk and enabling responsible financing for more than one million hectares.
